meta.label: Vitamin D
meta.what: UVB on uncovered skin starts vitamin D production. The estimate is rough, and more sun is not always better.

cases.html:
☀

Vitamin D

Not logged
No matching exposure was recorded this week. That is a logging result, not a deficiency.

UVB on uncovered skin starts vitamin D production. The estimate is rough, and more sun is not always better.

7-day rhythm sunlight · device

How to read it. This shows when vitamin-D-effective UVB reached uncovered skin. It is not a reason to stay outside longer.

Simple takeaway

This signal only appears when vitamin-D-effective UVB reaches uncovered skin. Its absence is not a prompt to extend exposure.

Research & sources

Spectrum: Pre-vitamin-D action spectrum (CIE 174:2006), peak ~298 nm UVB

  • Webb AR & Engelsen O (2006). "Calculated ultraviolet exposure levels for a healthy vitamin D status." Photochem Photobiol 82:1697
    Shows how vitamin-D-effective UV varies by place and season; the engine uses its spectral integral rather than a universal UVI cliff
  • Holick MF (2007). "Vitamin D Deficiency." NEJM 357:266
    Most-cited modern clinical review of the vitamin D pathway, including the per-session photoisomerization plateau (skin converts excess previtamin-D to inert tachysterol/lumisterol at high doses)
  • Bogh MK & Wulf HC (2010). "Vitamin D production after UVB exposure depends on baseline 25(OH)D and total cholesterol." J Invest Dermatol 130:546
    Shows large per-session response variability and why the IU-equivalent band must remain broad
Suggest a better study →

meta.label: Skin & mood
meta.what: Sunlight on skin can start signals involved in pigment, stress response, and how sunlight feels.

cases.html:
⚡

Skin & mood

Not logged
No matching exposure was recorded this week. That is a logging result, not a deficiency.

Sunlight on skin can start signals involved in pigment, stress response, and how sunlight feels.

7-day rhythm sunlight · device

How to read it. This shows light that may start the skin pathway. It does not measure hormones or mood.

Simple takeaway

This pathway appears when the relevant sunlight reaches logged skin. It is something to observe, not a UV goal.

Research & sources

Spectrum: UVA + UVB on skin keratinocytes → POMC → α-MSH/β-endorphin

  • Fell GL et al. (2014). "Skin β-endorphin mediates addiction to UV light." Cell 157:1527
    Landmark Cell paper showing UV → keratinocyte β-endorphin → opioid-receptor-mediated mood/addictive response
  • Slominski A et al. (2012). "Sensing the environment: regulation of local and global homeostasis by the skin's neuroendocrine system." Adv Anat Embryol Cell Biol 212:1
    Comprehensive review of skin as a neuroendocrine organ — POMC, α-MSH, ACTH, cortisol all expressed in skin
  • Cui R et al. (2007). "Central role of p53 in the suntan response and pathologic hyperpigmentation." Cell 128:853
    p53 → POMC → α-MSH → melanin pathway: the molecular mechanism behind the tan signal
Suggest a better study →

meta.label: Blood vessels
meta.what: UVA can release nitric oxide stored in skin, which may temporarily relax blood vessels.

cases.html:
❤

Blood vessels

Not logged
No matching exposure was recorded this week. That is a logging result, not a deficiency.

UVA can release nitric oxide stored in skin, which may temporarily relax blood vessels.

7-day rhythm sunlight · device

How to read it. This is a modeled skin-light signal, not a blood-pressure reading or a reason to seek more UVA.

Simple takeaway

This signal appears when UVA reaches logged skin. No signal means it was not modeled, not that your body is deficient.

Research & sources

Spectrum: UVA + violet (320-440 nm) on bare skin → photo-released NO

  • Liu D et al. (2014). "UVA irradiation of human skin vasodilates arterial vasculature and lowers blood pressure independently of nitric oxide synthase." J Invest Dermatol 134:1839
    Controlled mechanistic crossover trial showing UVA on skin lowers BP via photo-released NO from skin stores (NOT via vit-D)
  • Lindqvist PG et al. (2016). "Avoidance of sun exposure as a risk factor for major causes of death." J Intern Med 280:375
    Observational association over 20 years; it does not prove causality or make intentional UV exposure a treatment
  • Feelisch M et al. (2010). "Is sunlight good for our heart?" Eur Heart J 31:1041
    Foundational hypothesis paper laying out the UVA→NO→cardiovascular mechanism
Suggest a better study →

meta.label: Outdoor eye light
meta.what: Outdoor light includes violet wavelengths that are reduced by many windows. Their human effects are still being studied.

cases.html:
👁

Outdoor eye light

Not logged
No matching exposure was recorded this week. That is a logging result, not a deficiency.

Outdoor light includes violet wavelengths that are reduced by many windows. Their human effects are still being studied.

7-day rhythm sunlight · device

How to read it. This is an early-stage pathway model. Use normal ambient outdoor light and never stare at the sun.

Simple takeaway

A normal outdoor walk can provide ambient violet light. The human biology is still being studied.

Research & sources

Spectrum: Outdoor violet-light hypothesis, roughly 360–400 nm at the eye. Human evidence is stronger for time outdoors than for a wavelength-specific dose, and this is not a reason to expose unprotected eyes to UV.

  • Torii H et al. (2017). "Violet light exposure can be a preventive strategy against myopia progression." EBioMedicine 15:210
    Early human and experimental evidence for a violet-light hypothesis; it does not establish a safe eye-exposure dose
  • Rose KA et al. (2008). "Outdoor activity reduces the prevalence of myopia in children." Ophthalmology 115:1279
    Cohort of >4000 kids (1,765 six-year-olds + 2,367 twelve-year-olds): time outdoors (not near-work) is the protective factor against myopia
  • He M et al. (2015). "Effect of Time Spent Outdoors at School on the Development of Myopia Among Children in China: A Randomized Clinical Trial." JAMA 314:1142
    JAMA RCT in ~1,900 first-graders: 40 extra outdoor min/day cut new-myopia incidence by 9 percentage points (39.5% → 30.4%, ~23% relative reduction)
Suggest a better study →

Spectrum: Outdoor violet-light hypothesis, roughly 360–400 nm at the eye. Human evidence is stronger for time outdoors than for a wavelength-specific dose, and this is not a reason to expose unprotected eyes to UV.

  • Torii H et al. (2017). "Violet light exposure can be a preventive strategy against myopia progression." EBioMedicine 15:210
    Early human and experimental evidence for a violet-light hypothesis; it does not establish a safe eye-exposure dose
  • Rose KA et al. (2008). "Outdoor activity reduces the prevalence of myopia in children." Ophthalmology 115:1279
    Cohort of >4000 kids (1,765 six-year-olds + 2,367 twelve-year-olds): time outdoors (not near-work) is the protective factor against myopia
  • He M et al. (2015). "Effect of Time Spent Outdoors at School on the Development of Myopia Among Children in China: A Randomized Clinical Trial." JAMA 314:1142
    JAMA RCT in ~1,900 first-graders: 40 extra outdoor min/day cut new-myopia incidence by 9 percentage points (39.5% → 30.4%, ~23% relative reduction)

7-day rhythm sunlight · device

How to read it. This records red and near-infrared exposure. Sunlight and a targeted device are not treated as the same experience.

Simple takeaway

An outdoor session naturally includes red and near-infrared light as part of the wider daylight spectrum.

Research & sources

Spectrum: Red and near-infrared light, roughly 600–1400 nm. Sunlight and targeted devices are shown separately because their spectra and delivery are different.

  • "Longer wavelengths in sunlight pass through the human body and have a systemic impact which improves vision." Scientific Reports 15:24435 (2025)
    Human work measuring long-wave sunlight through the body and testing a separate 850 nm body exposure
  • "A Controlled Trial to Determine the Efficacy of Red and Near-Infrared Light Treatment." Photomed Laser Surg 32:93 (2014)
    A controlled study of broad red and near-infrared light for the specific skin outcomes tested
  • "Melatonin and the Optics of the Human Body." Melatonin Research 2:138 (2019)
    Introduces the proposed link between near-infrared light, body optics, and melatonin inside cells
  • Hamblin MR (2018). "Mechanisms and Mitochondrial Redox Signaling in Photobiomodulation." Photochem Photobiol 94:199
    Reviews several ways red and near-infrared light may interact with cell energy and signaling
